notes: Wikipedia lists series books #1-35 (1986-1997); no special or super edition was found in this span (the series collector edition is 1999). Book 35 location is unverified. Rows marked OUR anchor/guess in notes are design choices for unnamed or invented book places.

sites.name: THE SMELTER STACK FALLS
sites.shape: hard mining-and-rail town gone sour, a trade stop the convoys skirt because the core runs hot
sites.notes: Real city: a planned grid on the Missouri River with a chain of hydro dams over the falls (Rainbow, Ryan) and the stump of the ACM smelter stack (demolished 1982). The book only names a hot-spot city called "Grand Falls" on the convoy route; identifying it with Great Falls MT is OUR guess, flag as uncertain.

source.notes: a burned-out city on the convoy route that the trucks must detour around because it is still radioactive (identification with Great Falls is our guess)

sites.name: THE DROWNED INLET GRID
sites.shape: a coastal city taken by the sea, only rooftops and the high blocks above the tide flats
sites.notes: Real downtown is a gridded terrace above Cook Inlet tidal flats (Ship Creek, the rail yard and bluffs). The book says the city is gone, swallowed by the sea; build it as a flooded grid with the highest towers still standing.

source.notes: the crew finds the big coastal city wiped out and swallowed by the sea, so they turn north up the highway

sites.name: THE NORTHBOUND ROADHOUSE RUN
sites.shape: a lone two-lane highway north through spruce and snow, roadhouses and a single valley road
sites.notes: Real highway (AK-3) runs ~520 km from the Glenn Highway junction to Fairbanks through Mat-Su and the Nenana River corridor. Snow-buggy chase road; long straight with one river bridge chokepoint.

source.notes: the crew drives snow buggies up the northbound highway toward the inland city, with invaders blocking the only valley road

sites.name: THE WHITE DISH WATCHPOST
sites.shape: a sealed Cold War early-warning radar station holding a teleport bunker, now an invader camp
sites.notes: Real station: BMEWS site on the Parks Highway with three huge 50x122 m AN/FPS-50 reflector walls (removed 2001) and later a phased-array building; rail spur from the Alaska Railroad. The book has a domed Cold War early-warning station near a dam; using Clear as the anchor is OUR choice.

bunker.notes: sealed radar-era bunker with a teleport chamber; generator hall above, chamber below

source.notes: invaders from across the strait occupy a small domed early-warning station in a valley below a dam

sites.name: THE GLACIER LAKE SPILLWAY
sites.shape: a dam at the head of a glacier valley that can be blown to flood out the road below
sites.notes: Real: 1,424 ha glacier lake above Anchorage with hydro diversion and an older downstream diversion dam (removed 2018). The book dam is unnamed; Eklutna is OUR anchor for a glacier-valley dam. Set-piece: blow the dam, wave clears the valley road.

source.notes: the crew fires a missile at a valley dam and the wall of water sweeps the invaders camped on the river road away; a ghost town sits by the dam

sites.name: THE CHENA BEND OUTPOST
sites.shape: an inland river town on permafrost, last fuel and shelter at the end of the north road
sites.notes: Real: grid downtown on the Chena River with bridges at Cushman St, Garden Island cut off by Noyes Slough, rail yards at the north end of the Alaska Railroad. Book only aims for it ("head up the highway to Fairbanks"); they never confirm arriving, so treat as a destination stop.

source.notes: the inland city the crew heads for after finding the coast city drowned

sites.name: THE CYPRESS DROWNLANDS
sites.shape: endless cypress swamp with stilt shacks, airboat channels and a sealed bunker under a levee
sites.notes: Real basin: the largest US river swamp, crossed by straight dredged oil canals (30-50 m wide) and ringed by flood levees; abandoned towns like Bayou Chene lie buried under silt. Good for airboat chases and a drowned-church landmark.

source.notes: the crew leaves a bunker into a vast swamp, steals a swamp boat and is chased by swamp raiders

sites.name: THE BAYOU MOTOR-INN TOWN
sites.shape: a tyrant's town built around a fortified motor hotel on a bayou, besieged from the swamp
sites.notes: Real: low (3 m) city that grew along converging bayous (Terrebonne, Black, Little Bayou) with drawbridges; strung-out linear plan, raised cottages. The book town (invented name) is run from an old chain motel; Houma is OUR anchor for a south-Louisiana bayou town.

source.notes: a cruel ruler holds a swamp town from a fortified old motel; the crew joins rebels who ram the gate with a napalm-loaded swamp boat

sites.name: THE BLUE CALDERA RIM
sites.shape: a perfect blue volcanic lake ringed by cliffs, reached by one road and one boat landing
sites.notes: Real: caldera ~8-10 km across, lake 594 m deep, rim cliffs 150-600 m; the only shore access is the Cleetwood Cove trail (200 m drop); Rim Drive 53 km; Crater Lake Lodge (1915) on the south rim. Miniature: a 600 m slice of rim + one cove + the island in the distance.

source.notes: a radio signal draws the crew to the lake, where guards boat them across to the island hiding a deep science complex

sites.name: THE CINDER CONE VAULT
sites.shape: a cinder-cone island in a crater lake with an elevator down to a sealed lab under the lakebed
sites.notes: Real: cinder cone rising 230 m above the lake, 2113 m summit with a 30 m deep summit crater, dock at Governors Bay, two trails. Book has a complex far below the lake that blows and sets off an eruption.

bunker.notes: elevator shaft from island to a deep lab under the lakebed; amphibious-vehicle bay

source.notes: an elevator on the island drops to a lab far beneath the lake; the crew escapes in an amphibious truck as the place blows

sites.name: THE TIMBER-ROAD HAMLET
sites.shape: a timber hamlet with a gas station on the mountain road north to the crater lake, held by armed guards
sites.notes: Real: unincorporated mill hamlet on OR-62 on the Rogue River below Crater Lake, Prospect Hotel (1892, NRHP), small airstrip. The book town is invented (newspaper named "Ginnsburg Falls"); Prospect is OUR anchor because it sits on the real southern road to the lake.

source.notes: the crew walks down the mountain to a gas station and an armed small town that escorts them north to the lake

sites.name: THE MOHAWK LOCK GORGE
sites.shape: a stone mill town in a narrow river gorge with a giant canal lock and a hidden bunker off the river
sites.notes: Real: city on a rocky defile where the Mohawk drops 14 m in 1.6 km; Erie Canal Lock 17 (12.3 m lift, one of the highest); New York Central main line on the bank; stone textile mills. The book puts a bunker "a little ways off the Mohawk river" upstate; Little Falls is OUR anchor.

source.notes: the crew arrives through a bunker just off the Mohawk River upstate and sets off down toward the Hudson

sites.name: THE HUDSON FERRY LANDING
sites.shape: a river-landing village under wooded hills where travellers take to the big river south
sites.notes: Real: village with a well-defined Main Street at the mouth of Catskill Creek on the Hudson, Rip Van Winkle Bridge, West Shore rail line, Catskill escarpment to the west. The book only says they pass the Catskill hills going down the Hudson.

source.notes: the crew passes the Catskill hills on the way down the Hudson River by boat

sites.name: THE STOCKADE RIVER TOWN
sites.shape: a colonial stone-house town and a creek-mouth port, both in ruins along the river route
sites.notes: Real: three districts - Uptown Stockade (17th-c. stone houses, Old Dutch Church, courthouse), Midtown, and the Rondout waterfront on Rondout Creek. Book only notes "the ruins of Kingston" as they pass.

source.notes: the crew passes the ruins of the old river town on their way south

sites.name: THE CANYON OF TOWERS
sites.shape: a flooded city of broken towers run by street gangs, with creatures in the tunnels below
sites.notes: Real: Manhattan street grid (1811 Commissioners plan) - avenues ~280 m apart, cross streets ~80 m; 34th-59th St midtown core of towers; Fifth Ave spine. Miniature: 3x5 blocks with one avenue canyon. Building heights capped at 6 storeys means towers read as broken stubs.

source.notes: the crew crosses the gang-held ruined city; later returns to find it flooded, gang-run and full of reptile creatures in the sewers

sites.name: THE TOLL BRIDGE MILLS
sites.shape: a tiny river borough with stone mills where a gang charges a toll on the old bridge
sites.notes: Real: 1.6 km2 borough on the Delaware with the Prallsville Mills complex (1790 linseed mill, 1877 grist mill, 1850 saw mill, 1900 silo), the D&R Canal feeder towpath and the Centre Bridge-Stockton crossing. Book: the crew hits a toll bridge at the Delaware near "the ruins of Stockton".

source.notes: at the Delaware river near the ruined town the crew runs into a gang working a toll bridge

sites.name: THE BLUE RIDGE TURNPIKE GAP
sites.shape: a river town at an interstate exit under a long wooded ridge, on the old highway west
sites.notes: Real: borough on the Schuylkill at the foot of Blue Mountain, served by I-78 (Exit 29). The book says they cross the Blue Mountains and go down old Interstate 78; Hamburg is OUR anchor for that ridge crossing.

source.notes: the crew cuts across the blue mountains and travels down the old interstate toward the river city

sites.name: THE DOMED CAPITAL RUINS
sites.shape: a state capital in ruins on a wide river, a domed capitol on the hill and raiders in the rubble
sites.notes: Real: Susquehanna is ~1.6 km wide here with City Island midstream; State Capitol (1906) with 83 m dome; Market and State Street bridges; long Rockville stone-arch rail bridge upstream. Book: a pair of guides ambush the crew in the ruins with their gang.

source.notes: two treacherous guides try to hand the crew to a ragged gang in the ruined river capital

sites.name: THE SHENANDOAH HOMESTEAD TOWN
sites.shape: a valley town and family stronghold at the river forks where a usurper brother holds the seat
sites.notes: Real: town where the North and South Forks join to form the Shenandoah, at the north tip of Massanutten and the Blue Ridge (Skyline Drive start); colonial square at Chester & Main. The book makes it the hero's family seat; we keep only the shape: a fortified family manor town at a river fork.

source.notes: the leader returns to his valley home town to settle a blood debt with the brother who seized it

sites.name: THE STAR EARTHWORK MESA FORT
sites.shape: an adobe frontier fort on open grassland where a cavalry troop under a ruthless commander rides out
sites.notes: Real: three successive forts in the Mora valley on the Santa Fe Trail; ruins of the third fort are roofless adobe walls on stone foundations with brick copings and standing chimneys; the second fort (1861) was a star-shaped earthwork; Santa Fe Trail ruts remain. Book fort is in unnamed NM desert; Fort Union is OUR anchor.

source.notes: a regiment of horse soldiers from the past rides out of a desert fort; the crew allies with Apache warriors to ambush them in a ruined town

sites.name: THE CAVALRY HILL POST
sites.shape: an old limestone cavalry post on the river bluffs with a museum of horse-soldier relics and a cold mortuary bunker
sites.notes: Real: post at the confluence of the Smoky Hill and Republican rivers (forming the Kansas River); historic Main Post of native limestone barracks around a parade ground, US Cavalry Museum, Custer House; Custer Hill barracks to the north. Book 6 mentions a 7th Cavalry museum; book 20 a mortuary bunker in Kansas. Both anchors here are OUR guesses.

bunker.notes: wartime mortuary bunker: warehouse-sized refrigerated halls on the top level, teleport chamber below

source.notes: a cavalry museum figures in the horse-soldier backstory; later the crew lands in a Kansas bunker full of frozen bodies raided by cannibals (both anchored here by us)

sites.name: THE HIGH ISLE THOROUGHFARE
sites.shape: a rocky spruce island in the bay with a park shelter, a broken road and a sealed sea bunker
sites.notes: Real: 12.5 km2 island town, half in Acadia NP, village beside the Thoroughfare at Kimball Island, north-south ridge to Mount Champlain (160 m), Long Pond. Book: a sea bunker brings the crew here; a park plaque names the island.

bunker.notes: rambling partly flooded undersea complex reached from a shore hatch

source.notes: the crew emerges from an undersea bunker onto a park island, finds the road off it destroyed by quakes and must build something that floats

sites.name: THE GRANITE QUARRY HARBOR
sites.shape: a hard fishing and sailing port run by a ruthless sea captain, tall ships at a granite wharf
sites.notes: Real: harbor town at the south tip of Deer Isle, granite quarries (Crotch Island etc.) that supplied Brooklyn Bridge approaches; houses climb from the harbor; Steamboat Wharf west of the main harbor; nearest port to Isle au Haut. The book port is invented ("Consequence, Maine"); Stonington is OUR anchor.

source.notes: the crew steals a sailing ship from a harsh port to chase a captain who sails off with captives

sites.name: THE FIRST-LIGHT SUMMIT
sites.shape: a bald pink-granite summit over the sea with a sealed bunker deep inside the mountain
sites.notes: Real: 466 m summit on Mount Desert Island, highest on the US Atlantic coast, bald pink granite, summit road; a cog railway and hotel stood 1883-1895. The book puts a bunker "deep in the Cadillac mountain".

bunker.notes: deep granite bunker with control room and teleport chamber; exit high on the mountain

source.notes: a sextant reading puts the crew on top of a Maine park mountain with their bunker deep inside it

sites.name: THE CLEAR POND VALLEY
sites.shape: a glassy mountain lake under twin domes, a hidden valley institute reached by back trails
sites.notes: Real: glacial pond, clearest in Maine (13-18 m visibility), framed by the Bubbles (twin domes) at the north end, Rockefeller carriage roads with granite-faced bridges, the Jordan Pond House. The book institute and valley are invented; Jordan Pond is OUR anchor for the lake the crew camps by.

source.notes: the crew camps by a park lake, notices identical dogs, and is taken in by a reactivated medical institute in a hidden valley

sites.name: THE SIERRA FOOT FUEL TOWN
sites.shape: a high-desert town under a granite mountain wall rebuilding on gasoline money, run by a snake cult
sites.notes: Real: Owens Valley town at 1,130 m under Mount Whitney; 1872 quake left few pre-quake buildings (an "Old Adobe Wall"); Alabama Hills boulders west; dry Owens Lake south; charcoal and smelter history. The book town (invented name) is in "the Sierra Mountains" of southern California and rich in gasoline; Lone Pine is OUR anchor.

source.notes: a gasoline-rich rebuilding town in the southern California mountains is ruled through a snake-worshipping church; a city hall audience, a stolen snake and a raid

sites.name: THE BELOW-SEA OASIS
sites.shape: a palm oasis below sea level in a salt valley, a lonely outpost raided by mutants
sites.notes: Real: village at -58 m; Furnace Creek Inn (1927, stone and adobe terraces), palm oasis, Harmony Borax Works ruins, world-record heat (56.7 C). Book: "a base near Death Valley" raided by mutants twice.

source.notes: an outpost near the great hot valley is raided twice by mutants and a sacred snake goes missing

sites.name: THE WEAPONS RANGE AIRFIELD

real.place: Naval Air Weapons Station China Lake

sites.shape: a desert weapons-test base, runways and test bunkers on a dry lake, picked over by raiders
sites.notes: Real: >4,500 km2 base; Armitage Field with three runways built for B-29s (3,000/2,300/2,700 m); range bunkers. This is OUR anchor for the book's unnamed "base near Death Valley".

bunker.notes: range test bunker and a sealed lower level; not a confirmed book teleport site

source.notes: the mountain town mentions a base near the hot valley being raided by mutants (anchored here by us)

sites.name: THE NAVY RANGE ISLAND
sites.shape: a bare offshore island with a sealed bunker, a booby-trapped game room and a raft-crossing to the mainland
sites.notes: Real: Navy-owned Channel Island, the Navy's only remaining ship-to-shore live-fire range, airfield in the north, steep eastern scarp and marine terraces in the west, Pyramid Cove whaling history in the south. The book only says "an island near the coast of California"; San Clemente is OUR anchor. Mainland sulfur springs and a pig canyon follow.

bunker.notes: soldiers' bunker with dorms, an arcade room (booby-trapped), control room and teleport chamber

source.notes: the crew finds a bunker with a booby-trapped arcade game on an island off California, rafts to the mainland and falls in with brushland raiders and wild pigs

sites.name: THE BIRCHWOOD DACHA VILLAGE
sites.shape: a half-burned country house in a birch-wood dacha village, a secret stair down to a tiny teleport room
sites.notes: Real: writers' dacha settlement SW of Moscow among birch and pine woods, wooden dachas (Pasternak house museum), church and cemetery, suburban rail halt. The book has an American-owned dacha in the Moscow suburbs; Peredelkino is OUR anchor.

source.notes: the crew climbs a spiral stair out of a cramped teleport room into the chimney of a half-burned country house near the enemy capital

sites.name: THE TROPHY HALL MUSEUM
sites.shape: a grand military museum with captured enemy relics where the crew must steal tools and a flag at night
sites.notes: Real: museum on Sovetskoy Armii St with 24 halls and an open-air yard of tanks, aircraft and missiles; Cold War hall shows the U-2 wreck. The book "war museum" is generic; this real museum is OUR anchor.

source.notes: the crew tours an enemy war museum to find stolen tools, then breaks in at night to take the tools and a captured flag

sites.name: THE TWIN-BAY LONGHOUSE SHORE
sites.shape: a warrior village of longhouses and longships on the shore of the great cold lake, jungle behind
sites.notes: Real: harbor town on Lake Superior's North Shore with two bays, Artist's Point lava tombolo and breakwall lighthouse, Pincushion Mountain bald monolith behind. The book puts warrior settlers "on the shore of Lake Superior" in a tropical Minnesota; Grand Marais is OUR anchor.

source.notes: in a jungle-hot Minnesota the crew finds a village of sea-raider warriors on the great lake shore, then steals a boat east

sites.name: THE GARDEN WALL ICEFIELD
sites.shape: a shrinking glacier in a high cirque, a remembered hiking place above a mountain bunker
sites.notes: Real: glacier on Mount Gould's north flank at ~2,100 m in the Many Glacier area, shrank from 2.9 km2 (1850) to 0.89 km2 (1993); 9.7 km hike from Swiftcurrent Lake; Gem Glacier above on the Garden Wall. MENTION ONLY: the book recalls hiking here near a bunker; the crew does not visit in this span.

source.notes: a character remembers hiking to this glacier, the same area as a known bunker (mentioned, not visited)

sites.name: THE ADOBE PLAZA TRADE TOWN
sites.shape: a rich adobe trade town around a fortified plaza, fuel and ammo traded with a ruler and armed horsemen
sites.notes: Real: town built as a fortified plaza of adobe buildings, now the Taos Downtown Historic District, Bent Street, Ranchos de Taos plaza with the buttressed San Francisco de Asis church 6 km south. The book town name is a respelling of Taos "near what was once Albuquerque"; we use the real town.

source.notes: a trading convoy rolls into a wealthy adobe town to trade fuel and ammo with its ruler; a hunt for a white mountain lion follows

sites.name: THE FIVE-TIER EARTH PUEBLO
sites.shape: a terraced earth-house pueblo of armed tribesmen at the foot of a sacred mountain
sites.notes: Real: two multi-storey adobe house blocks (north and south) of up to 5 stacked storeys either side of Red Willow Creek, inside a low adobe wall, with San Geronimo church and the ruined old church and cemetery. Architecture is the real thing; the book only mentions armed Apaches near the town (do not depict real Taos people as hostile).

source.notes: armed Apache riders share the high valley with the adobe trade town

sites.name: THE RIVER VALLEY SPRAWL RUINS
sites.shape: a sprawling desert city in ruins along a green river under a granite mountain wall, picked for a buried bunker
sites.notes: Real: city from 1,508 m at the Rio Grande to 1,879 m in the Sandia foothills; Old Town plaza (1706) of adobe around San Felipe de Neri; Central Ave (Route 66) strip; Sandia Crest 3,255 m. Book: the crew searches ruins near the city for a hidden bunker.

source.notes: the crew recons ruins near the big desert city looking for a hidden bunker

sites.name: THE BASALT GORGE SPAN
sites.shape: a steel arch bridge flung across a sheer basalt gorge on the high mesa, a natural chokepoint
sites.notes: Real: steel deck arch bridge (1965) 16 km NW of Taos, spans 91-183-91 m, roughly 180 m above the river in a basalt gorge. Not named in the book; included as a real landmark on the route north of the trade town where the book has the crew camp by a river. OUR addition, flag as not-book.

source.notes: (real landmark on the high road near the trade town; the book only mentions camping by a river)

sites.name: THE RED CLIFF BOX-CANYON RANCH
sites.shape: a remote ranch in red cliff box canyons near a sealed bunker; a peaceful home that raiders burn
sites.notes: Real: 85 km2 ranch in the Chama valley of Rio Arriba County: banded red, yellow and white cliffs, box canyons once used by rustlers, flat-topped Cerro Pedernal on the skyline; adobe ranch buildings. The book home ranch and nearby bunker are unlocated in "the red-baked mountains of New Mexico"; Ghost Ranch is OUR anchor (the series name-checks a painter famous for this landscape).

bunker.notes: the surface of this bunker is obliterated; the teleport chamber below still works

source.notes: the crew's friend settles a ranch near a bunker in the NM mountains; a son is kidnapped from it, it is later attacked, and a manhunt across the canyon lands starts here

sites.name: THE GREAT HOUSE ARC
sites.shape: ancient multi-storey stone great-house ruins in a canyon, now a lair for mutant captors
sites.notes: Real: D-shaped great house of ~650 rooms up to 4-5 storeys of core-and-veneer sandstone (walls ~0.9 m), a N-S wall splitting the plaza, many round kivas, and the collapsed 30 m Threatening Rock slab behind (fell 1941). The book says "ancient Anasazi ruins" in NM; Pueblo Bonito is OUR anchor.

source.notes: mutant captors hold prisoners in ancient pueblo ruins in the NM desert; the crew follows a river north to their camp

sites.name: THE CANYON-MOUTH FRONTIER POST
sites.shape: a frontier army post tucked in a rock-walled canyon in the West Texas mountains, a wagon-train stop
sites.notes: Real: 1854 post tucked into a canyon flanked on three sides by rock walls; rebuilt after 1867 in limestone and adobe outside the canyon walls; officers' row faces the parade ground. The book is in "the southwest desert near the NM-Texas border" with a cruel ranch family and a wagon train heading south; Fort Davis is OUR anchor.

source.notes: stranded in West Texas the crew joins a wagon train heading south that holds a grim lottery; a revenge-hunter tracks them

sites.name: THE HIGH DESERT RAILROAD RANCH TOWN
sites.shape: a high-desert rail and ranch town around a domed courthouse, home of a cruel ranch family
sites.notes: Real: 1880s railroad water stop at 1,428 m on high grassland between the Davis Mountains and Big Bend; Presidio County Courthouse (1886) domed Second Empire; WWII army airfield east of town. The book ranch is unnamed; Marfa is OUR anchor for a West Texas ranch-family town.

source.notes: the crew frees a young woman from her brutal father and brothers on a West Texas ranch

sites.name: THE RIVERBANK BROWNSTONE GRID
sites.shape: a dense brownstone grid on the far riverbank where a bunker shaft opens into a wrecked Victorian house
sites.notes: Real: 2-mile-square city on the Hudson facing Manhattan, masonry rowhouses of 3-5 storeys on a preserved street grid, the Lackawanna rail/ferry terminal (1907, clock tower), riverside walkway. The book only says the bunker shaft opens into a destroyed Victorian house in a destroyed city across the river from Manhattan, crossed by a family ferry; Hoboken is OUR anchor.

source.notes: the crew climbs from a bunker into a wrecked Victorian house, meets a teen gang member and pays a ruthless family ferry to cross into the island city

sites.name: THE HAWK-TURF TENEMENT BLOCKS
sites.shape: gang turf of burned brick tenements and warehouses beside the river, one gang's hideouts
sites.notes: Real: industrial area below E 138th St growing north; 1970s arson left gutted 5-6 storey brick walk-ups; the 41st Precinct station-house nicknamed "Fort Apache"; Cross Bronx Expressway trench; Harlem River yards. Book: a teen leads the crew to his gang's hideout here beside lizard-mutant territory.

source.notes: a teenage gang member takes the crew to his gang's hideout in the burned northern borough next to reptile-mutant turf

sites.name: THE SWING BRIDGE STRAIT
sites.shape: a narrow tidal strait of swing bridges and dockside warehouses, the boat route to a hidden bunker
sites.notes: Real: 13 km tidal strait between Manhattan and the Bronx with seven swing, four lift and four arch bridges; High Bridge (1848) stone aqueduct is the oldest bridge in NYC. Book: lizard mutants hold the old warehouses by the river and the crew boats down it to reach the hidden bunker.

source.notes: reptile mutants hold the dockside warehouses; the crew escapes by boat up the strait to their hidden bunker

sites.name: THE MEADOW MARKET PARK
sites.shape: a huge city park turned into an open-air market under the ruined skyline, neutral ground between gangs
sites.notes: Real: 59th-110th St x 5th-8th Ave (4 km x 0.8 km), sunken transverse roads at 66th/79th/86th/97th, Bethesda Terrace and Fountain at 72nd, the Lake with cast-iron Bow Bridge, the Ramble, Manhattan schist outcrops. Miniature: the Terrace-Lake-Ramble slice.

source.notes: the crew reaches the great park, now a huge open-air market, where two of them are ambushed and taken by reptile mutants

sites.name: THE AVENUE OF MUSEUMS
sites.shape: a line of stone museums and mansions along the park where an underground lord hoards prewar treasures
sites.notes: Real: Fifth Ave from 82nd to 105th along Central Park: the Met (Beaux-Arts limestone), the Guggenheim (spiral concrete, 89th), Neue Galerie, Cooper Hewitt in mansions. The book names the avenue and the spiral museum and an underground ruler with prewar memorabilia.

source.notes: an underground ruler beneath the city keeps a fortress filled with prewar treasures and lends the crew a scout vehicle

sites.name: THE NEON ROLLER COAST
sites.shape: a still-standing theme park in a swamp jungle rebuilt as a ruler's seat, rides that still run
sites.notes: Real: I-Drive is Orlando's 4-6 lane tourism corridor of hotels, attractions and theme parks between I-4 and the parks; theme parks are reinforced-concrete show buildings with steel coasters. The book park and its name are invented ("well-kept remains of a large theme park" in a Florida swamp); we use the Orlando park belt generically, NO real park brands.

source.notes: in a Florida swamp jungle the crew is disarmed at a well-kept theme park ruled by a crippled old enemy controlled by a drug-dealing sociopath

sites.name: THE CORAL KEY RESEARCH DOCK
sites.shape: a long coral-rock key with a marine research institute that hires the crew to hold off pirates
sites.notes: Real: longest Key, a coral-limestone ridge at most ~4.6 m high, no natural beaches, mangroves on the bay side and the reef offshore; CDPs North Key Largo, Key Largo, Tavernier strung along US-1. The book institute is invented and its key unnamed ("the chain from Key Largo to Key West"); Key Largo is OUR anchor.

source.notes: an oceanographic institute in the Keys hires the crew for five days to defend it against pirates

sites.name: THE LONG SPAN CROSSING
sites.shape: two parallel ocean bridges, one broken, linking keys over open water - a duel lane for boats and cars
sites.notes: Real: new bridge (1982) beside the 1909-12 Flagler railroad bridge with a removed swing span over Moser Channel; Pigeon Key work-camp island sits under the old bridge. Not named in the book; included because the book route spans the whole chain (OUR addition).

source.notes: (the chain of keys the book describes is linked by this real long bridge; not named in the book)

sites.name: THE SOUTHERNMOST PIER TOWN
sites.shape: the last island town: wood houses on piers, forts and a sealed motel where a strange tribe lives
sites.notes: Real: island averaging 2.4 m elevation (max 5.5 m Solares Hill); wood-frame houses of 1-2.5 storeys raised ~1 m on piers; Mallory Square, Duval Street, Fort Zachary Taylor, East and West Martello towers. The book says a peculiar mutant group lives in a near-perfect chain motel "on a southern island"; Key West is OUR anchor.

source.notes: scouting the southern keys the crew finds an odd tribe living in a spotless old chain motel

sites.name: THE CHARRED LOOP GRID
sites.shape: a great lakeside city burned nearly flat, a sealed bunker under it with a working armored truck
sites.notes: Real: the Loop is 35 blocks inside the elevated rail ring (Lake, Wells, Van Buren, Wabash); State & Madison is the origin of the city grid; blocks ~100 m. Book: city leveled to a flat charred wasteland; the crew finds a bunker beneath it and drives out in a large armored truck.

bunker.notes: large bunker under the city with a vehicle garage; giant spiders in the lower levels

source.notes: beneath the leveled lakeside city the crew finds a bunker garage with a working armored truck and explores the charred ruins

sites.name: THE BASCULE RIVER CANYON
sites.shape: a walled city river under dozens of lift bridges, a fast cold channel to fall into
sites.notes: Real: main stem runs 2.4 km west from the lake locks under the Lake Shore, Columbus, Michigan, Wabash, State, Dearborn, Clark, LaSalle, Wells and Franklin bascule bridges to the fork at Wolf Point; walled concrete banks. Book: a fight ends with a fall into a rock-strewn rapid river and a rescue.

source.notes: during a night chase one of the crew falls into a fast river and is pulled out by a stranger

sites.name: THE LAKESHORE FOUNTAIN PARK
sites.shape: a grand lakefront park and harbor between the burned towers and the inland sea
sites.notes: Real: 1.29 km2 park between Michigan Ave and Lake Michigan (Randolph to Roosevelt), Buckingham Fountain, the Art Institute, Logan monument hill, DuSable Harbor (420 slips). OUR addition: the book explores the city ruins generally; this is the lake edge of the same miniature.

source.notes: (lake edge of the burned city the crew explores in an armored truck)

sites.name: THE TIMBERLINE GHOST CAMP
sites.shape: a snowbound high-country mining camp near an icy mountain bunker, a feudal valley lord and a bandit town over the ridge
sites.notes: Real: 1879 gold camp at 3,326 m, 3.6 km below Independence Pass on CO-82, 17-acre townsite with 19 surviving buildings and 9 foundations, Farwell Stamp Mill ruin. The books put an icy bunker and two feuding towns somewhere in the snowy Colorado Rockies (both town names are invented); Independence is OUR anchor.

bunker.notes: small stripped icy bunker; one corridor broken open to the mountainside by an earthquake

source.notes: the crew arrives in an icy Rockies bunker, kills a giant bear, and is forced by a grief-mad valley ruler to hunt his enemy in a bandit town; later the leader climbs the frozen mountain to re-enter the bunker

sites.name: THE HOT POOL CONFLUENCE
sites.shape: a canyon-mouth spa town at a river fork, steaming pools and a grand old hotel, a supply stop
sites.notes: Real: town at the confluence of the Roaring Fork and Colorado rivers at the mouth of Glenwood Canyon; Hotel Colorado (1893, Italian villa style), a 1888 hot springs pool and red sandstone bathhouse lodge; Pioneer Cemetery above Bennett Ave; rail depot. Book: supply stop and a diner fight.

source.notes: the crew stops at the nearest town for supplies; a bad diner meal ends in a fight and a fire

sites.name: THE COLORADO RIVER SLOT ROAD
sites.shape: a deep river canyon with a stacked highway and rail line on ledges, a cliff road for wagons and ambushes
sites.notes: Real: 20 km canyon with I-70 on stacked and cantilevered decks, the rail line on the opposite bank, Shoshone dam and hydro plant, Hanging Lake tunnel. The book wagon goes over a cliff on the road toward the mining city (route not named); OUR road-hazard addition.

source.notes: (the cliff road out of the spa town toward the high mining city, where bandits send a wagon over the edge)

sites.name: THE CLOUD CITY SILVER CAMP
sites.shape: a two-mile-high silver city of brick and false fronts ringed by mine dumps, a trade terminus
sites.notes: Real: town at 3,096 m near timberline; Harrison Avenue main street with the 1879 Tabor Opera House (3 storeys of stone, brick and iron) and courthouse; mine dumps on the east hills; Mount Massive and Elbert west. Book: a merchant hauls a piano up to it.

source.notes: the leader and his son ride guard on a merchant hauling a piano up to the high mining city

sites.name: THE SOUTH PARK BLUFF TOWN
sites.shape: a high-basin gold town on a river bluff, the meeting point for a split-up crew
sites.notes: Real: town at 3,034 m in the South Park basin; historic town on the bluff above the Middle Fork of the South Platte along Front Street; Park County Courthouse; dredge tailings along the river. Book: the agreed meeting place before the last leg home.

source.notes: the crew splits up and agrees to meet at the high-basin town before going on together

sites.name: THE TENTH VALLEY BARRACKS
sites.shape: a ruined mountain-troop training camp in a flat high meadow, on the road between the spa town and the silver city
sites.notes: Real: WWII 10th Mountain Division camp at 2,815 m in the Eagle River valley between Red Cliff and Leadville near Tennessee Pass; white barracks for 15,000 in straight lines on the meadow (only foundations remain); later CIA training site. OUR route guess - not named in the book; the book only has a road trip toward Leadville.

bunker.notes: speculative: a small sealed store under the old camp, not a book site

source.notes: (real abandoned army camp on one road between the spa town and the silver city; not named in the book)

sites.name: THE CASCADE SUMMIT GAP
sites.shape: a forested mountain pass with a lake and a dead rail tunnel where the old mentor is found camped
sites.notes: Real: pass at 919 m on the King/Kittitas line, I-90 and Lake Keechelus on the east side, the 3.6 km Snoqualmie rail tunnel (1914, now a trail), ski areas. The book only says "wandering through the Cascade Mountains"; Snoqualmie is OUR anchor on the Seattle road.

source.notes: two of the crew wander the Cascade Mountains and find their old mentor alive with his companion

sites.name: THE RAIN-TOWER MALL DISTRICT
sites.shape: a steep rain-soaked city of ruined towers and a dead shopping mall where norm gangs shadow outsiders
sites.notes: Real: downtown on steep hills rising from Elliott Bay; grid skewed between two street systems; terra-cotta early towers (Pioneer Square) and glass towers; Pike Place Market arcade; Alaskan Way viaduct on the waterfront (demolished 2019; present c.2000); Westlake area malls. Book: the crew walks into the ruins, holes up in a house, searches a mall and is shadowed out by a gang.

source.notes: the crew walks into the rain-city ruins, finds little, searches a mall and is shadowed out of town by a gang

sites.name: THE HILL CROWN HOUSES
sites.shape: a hilltop neighborhood of big old frame houses and stairs where travellers hole up for the night
sites.notes: Real: steep hill north of downtown between Lake Union and Elliott Bay; Queen Anne Boulevard loops the crown (Olmsted style); old frame houses; broadcast towers on the summit. OUR anchor for the book's unnamed "old house" where the crew holes up.

source.notes: the crew holes up in an old house on the edge of the ruins for the night

sites.name: THE APPLE VALLEY RAIL TOWN
sites.shape: a dry irrigated valley town east of the mountains, orchards and rail sheds, where the wagon breaks a wheel
sites.notes: Real: 1,095 ft (334 m) valley city on the Yakima River, downtown moved wholesale in 1884 to the Northern Pacific depot (rail-oriented grid), fruit-packing warehouses along the tracks, orchards in West Valley.

source.notes: near the valley town east of the mountains the funeral-car wagon hits a pothole and shatters a wheel

sites.name: THE RIM HOTEL LEDGE
sites.shape: a log-and-stone rim hotel and rail depot on the canyon lip, seat of a degenerate canyon lord
sites.notes: Real: South Rim village with El Tovar (1905, log and stone, Santa Fe Railway), the log Grand Canyon Depot (1909), Lookout Studio and Kolb Studio on the rim edge, Bright Angel trailhead. The book has a building near the canyon top with a balcony and a degenerate ruling family; El Tovar is OUR anchor.

source.notes: after riding a flood through the rapids, the crew climbs to a building by the canyon top held by a degenerate ruling family; a woman falls from a balcony into the canyon

sites.name: THE INNER GORGE RIVER CAMP
sites.shape: a stone camp on the canyon floor by suspension footbridges over a rising river during a quake
sites.notes: Real: 1922 Mary Colter-designed river-stone cabins and canteen at 750 m by Bright Angel Creek, the Black (Kaibab) and Silver (Bright Angel) suspension bridges over the Colorado; CCC corral and an old pool. The book camp in the canyon is unnamed; Phantom Ranch is OUR anchor. Set-piece: a quake raises the river, two cross a bridge, two ride a floating tree downstream.

source.notes: camped in the great canyon, the group is split by an earthquake and a rising river; two cross by a bridge, two ride a floating tree through the rapids

sites.name: THE SUN BASIN SUBDIVISIONS
sites.shape: a vast desert suburb of stucco houses and empty canals, a safe-ish night stop on the way home
sites.notes: Real: 1,341 km2 city at 331 m in the Sonoran Desert on the Salt River, laid on a mile-square section grid crossed by old Hohokam-line irrigation canals; postwar single-storey stucco suburbs with block walls. Book: the crew spends a night in a relatively intact suburb.

source.notes: the crew reaches the desert city and spends a quiet night in an intact suburb before heading home

sites.name: THE LAKESHORE BOMBER BASE
sites.shape: a lakeside bomber base with old stone barracks and a crude bunker cut into granite
sites.notes: Real: 1814 Plattsburgh Barracks (1838 Old Stone Barracks and powder magazine survive) became a SAC bomber base (13.7 km2) on the west shore of Lake Champlain opposite Burlington; closed 1995. The book bunker (hastily cut into granite) is near "Lake Champlain" in New England; this base is OUR anchor.

bunker.notes: hastily built control chamber carved from a granite cave; misaligned doors and glass

source.notes: the crew arrives in a badly built bunker cut into granite near the big northern lake and finds a hidden valley of eternally young people

sites.name: THE CHAMPLAIN TERRACE TOWN
sites.shape: a lake-port town climbing from the shore to a hilltop college, a sanctuary town ruled by a prophet
sites.notes: Real: city on a strip of land running ~9.7 km south from the Winooski mouth, rising 91 m from the lake to the University of Vermont green; Church Street brick downtown; railroad causeway into the lake. The book town is invented; Burlington is OUR anchor for a lakeside town by the bunker.

source.notes: by the northern lake the crew finds a town of the healthy and young, led by a prophet with a temple full of famous paintings; a dark price lies beneath

sites.name: THE CRATER MALL
sites.shape: a blast crater where the capital's grand lawn was, monuments half-buried, shanty towns ringing the edge
sites.notes: Real: 3 km mall from the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial, 483 m wide at 7th St; museums along both sides; Washington Monument (169 m marble obelisk) at the center-west. The book city has become a great blast crater with shanty towns around it; we keep "a crater where the capital mall was", never the book's coined name.

source.notes: the crew comes out near the great crater where the capital stood and visits the shanty towns around it; a tornado splits the group

sites.name: THE PRESIDENT'S BURNED LAWN
sites.shape: a white sandstone mansion behind iron fences, roof gone, the grounds a squatter camp at the crater edge
sites.notes: Real: Federal/Neoclassical sandstone mansion (painted white) on a timber-then-steel frame (gutted and rebuilt 1949-52), East and West Wings, Treasury Building east, Pennsylvania Ave closed to cars since 1995, Lafayette Park north. Named in the book only via an epigraph about the city.

source.notes: (the book opens by remembering the capital's mansion; the crew roams the ruins around the crater)

sites.name: THE COLUMNED TEMPLE AT THE POOL
sites.shape: a marble temple above a long reflecting pool at the end of the drowned mall
sites.notes: Real: Doric temple of 36 columns, interior three chambers divided by Ionic columns 15 m tall; 87 steps descend to the Reflecting Pool; Memorial Bridge to the west over the Potomac. Named in the book only via the opening epigraph.

source.notes: (named in the book's opening quote about the capital's monuments)

sites.name: THE ROWHOUSE HILL SHANTIES
sites.shape: a hill of brick rowhouses and churches around the crater, an inn run by an old acquaintance, ambushes in the streets
sites.notes: Real: rowhouse district of ~5 km2 east of the Capitol: 19th-c. Federal and Italianate rowhouses and late-Victorian press-brick rows (Romanesque, Queen Anne); L'Enfant grid cut by diagonal avenues (Pennsylvania Ave) with square parks; Eastern Market (1873), Marine Barracks. OUR anchor for the shanty towns and the inn around the crater.

source.notes: the crew stays at an inn in the shanty towns ringing the crater, sees a fortune-teller and shoots its way out when plain-clothes guards attack

sites.name: THE NICHE PYRAMID JUNGLE
sites.shape: a jungle village under a stepped stone pyramid, slavers on the trails and an abandoned army base nearby
sites.notes: Real: pre-Hispanic city in the Veracruz lowlands; the Pyramid of the Niches (365 niches, stepped tiers, on a 3,000 m2 platform), ~20 ball courts (one 60x10.5 m), greca stepped-fret walls. The book is only "somewhere in the tropics" with a pyramid sacrifice and slavers; El Tajín is OUR anchor and the tribe is invented - depict it as a fictional post-collapse tribe, not a real people.

source.notes: in a hot jungle the crew helps a village against slavers and a rival tribe, burns out an army-ant swarm with fuel from an abandoned army base, and rescues one of their own from sacrifice atop a pyramid

sites.name: THE LIVE-OAK ALLEE MANSION
sites.shape: a columned river-road mansion at the end of a live-oak tunnel, home of a pale night-feeding family
sites.notes: Real: 1837-39 Greek Revival mansion with 28 Doric columns on all four sides, at the end of an ~240 m double row of 28 live oaks planted before the house, facing the Mississippi levee on the River Road. The book house is in the Louisiana bayous (invented town); Oak Alley is OUR anchor; the slavery history of the site must be handled respectfully.

source.notes: down a path from the bunker into the bayous, the crew finds a family of vampire-like killers in an old house near a river town

sites.name: THE LIMESTONE CASTLE TERRACES
sites.shape: a hilltop warlord's fortress of curving stone walls on a subtropical island, samurai and a teleport room under a house
sites.notes: Real: Hokuzan-kingdom gusuku on the Motobu Peninsula, ~1.5 km of curving limestone walls in terraced enclosures over the East China Sea, a harbor inlet below; burned by Satsuma in 1609. The book says the crew is in Japan, the computers labelled in Japanese, with a warlord's fortress; a link names the Ryukyu islands, so Okinawa is OUR (reasonable) anchor.

source.notes: the crew is taken in by a warlord in his island fortress, fights an assassin ninja, and marches north against renegade samurai

sites.name: THE SEAWALL STRIP OF FOREIGN STORES
sites.shape: a seaside strip of foreign-style stores, a golf course and a resort hotel where a poison-gas trap is sprung
sites.notes: Real: town on the west coast by Kadena, home of American Village (malls, arcades, a big Ferris wheel), a 25-storey beach hotel, Sunabe sea wall; limestone hills inland. The book coast road passes American stores, a truncated golf course and a hotel ballroom; Chatan is OUR anchor.

source.notes: the warlord's march passes American stores and a cut-off golf course and stops at a hotel, where renegades lock the ballroom and pump in poison gas

sites.name: THE COTTON BLUFF COURT
sites.shape: a river-bluff city where a beautiful sorceress-ruler holds court above the great river
sites.notes: Real: downtown rises from a bluff over the Mississippi; Cotton Row warehouses on Front St, the cobblestone landing, Mud Island harbor, the Peabody (1925, grand hotel), Victorian Village mansions, Harahan/Frisco truss bridges. The book is only "a Tennessee town on the Mississippi"; Memphis is OUR anchor.

source.notes: the crew are guests of a powerful Tennessee ruler and her mysterious adviser at her town on the great river

sites.name: THE UNDER-THE-HILL LANDING
sites.shape: a river landing below a high bluff where a gambling paddle-steamer docks; the stakes turn deadly
sites.notes: Real: city on a ~60 m loess bluff with deep ravines ("bayous"); Natchez-Under-the-Hill is the old riverfront landing (saloons, a casino boat in the 1990s) at the foot of Silver Street; antebellum mansions on top; twin cantilever bridges to Vidalia. The book riverboat is unplaced on the Mississippi; Natchez is OUR anchor.

source.notes: the crew boards a gambling riverboat on the great river; a genial captain's games escalate until the leader is sold to the highest bidder

sites.name: THE FOUR STONE FACES VAULT
sites.shape: four colossal carved faces on a granite peak with a sealed technology vault inside the mountain
sites.notes: Real: granite peak (1,745 m) carved 1927-41 with 18 m faces; 517 ha memorial; Avenue of Flags and Grand View Terrace (rebuilt 1990s); the Hall of Records chamber cut behind the heads (sealed 1998); Borglum's studio. Book: the faces still stand and a ruler forces the crew to breach a mountain stronghold holding prewar technology.

bunker.notes: icy stronghold in the mountain with a cache of 20th-century technology and a surprise sleeper

source.notes: on sacred land the crew finds the carved mountain still standing; a charismatic ruler forces them to break into the frozen stronghold inside it

sites.name: THE GULCH MINING RESORT
sites.shape: a narrow-gulch mining-turned-tourist town at the foot of the carved mountain, the ruler's camp
sites.notes: Real: 1883 mining town in a narrow gulch on Battle Creek, now a resort strip serving Mount Rushmore 3 km away; heavily damaged in the 1972 flood; 1880 Train steam line runs to Hill City. OUR anchor for the ruler's base below the mountain.

source.notes: (the town below the carved mountain where the ruler and followers gather)

sites.name: THE LIMESTONE PRAIRIE MANOR
sites.shape: a ruler's art-filled manor town in rolling Kansas hills, hospitable by day, manhunts by night
sites.notes: Real: rolling tallgrass upland on chert-bearing limestone that resisted the plough; native-limestone barns, houses and stone fence posts; Tallgrass Prairie Preserve near Strong City. Note the book calls Kansas a hilly PINE forest, which doesn't match any real Kansas landscape; Flint Hills is OUR closest anchor for "hilly Kansas".

source.notes: in a hilly Kansas forest the crew is warmly hosted by a ruler with a famous-paintings collection, until they learn his hunting parties hunt men
